questions.question_text:
In an Entity-Relationship (ER) model, suppose 𝑅 is a many-to-one relationship from entity
set E1 to entity set E2. Assume that E1 and E2 participate totally in 𝑅 and that the cardinality
of E1 is greater than the cardinality of E2.

Which one of the following is true about 𝑅?

options.A: Every entity in E1 is associated with exactly one entity in E2.
options.B: Some entity in E1 is associated with more than one entity in E2.
options.C: Every entity in E2 is associated with exactly one entity in E1.
options.D: Every entity in E2 is associated with at most one entity in E1.

questions.subtopic: ER-model
questions.explaination: In an ER diagram, a many-to-one relationship from $E_1$ to $E_2$ means each entity in $E_1$ is related to at most one entity in $E_2$. Total participation of $E_1$ requires that every entity in $E_1$ participates in at least one relationship. Combining these, every entity in $E_1$ is associated with exactly one entity in $E_2$.
questions.question_text_latex: In an Entity-Relationship (ER) model, suppose $R$ is a many-to-one relationship from entity set $E_1$ to entity set $E_2$. Assume that $E_1$ has total participation in $R$, but $E_2$ has partial participation in $R$. Which one of the following statements is necessarily TRUE?

options_latex.A: Every entity in $E_1$ is associated with exactly one entity in $E_2$.
options_latex.B: Some entity in $E_1$ is associated with more than one entity in $E_2$.
options_latex.C: Every entity in $E_2$ is associated with at least one entity in $E_1$.
options_latex.D: Every entity in $E_2$ is associated with at most one entity in $E_1$.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following two tables and four queries in SQL.
Book (isbn, bname), Stock (isbn, copies)

Query 1: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B INNER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Query 2: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B LEFT OUTER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Query 3: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B RIGHT OUTER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Query 4: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B FULL OUTER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Which one of the queries above is certain to have an output that is a superset of the outputs
of the other three queries?
questions.subtopic: Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL
questions.explaination: Query 1 uses natural join (inner join), Query 2 uses left outer join, Query 3 uses right outer join, and Query 4 uses full outer join. A full outer join preserves all tuples from both relation $Book$ and relation $Stock$ (filling missing values with NULLs). Therefore, every tuple output by Query 1, Query 2, and Query 3 is guaranteed to appear in Query 4.

options_latex.A: Query 1 and Query 2 always produce the same number of rows.
options_latex.B: Query 2 and Query 3 always produce the same number of rows.
options_latex.C: Query 1 always produces the maximum number of rows among all queries.
options_latex.D: All rows from Query 1, Query 2, and Query 3 are always present in the result of Query 4.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following four relational schemas. For each schema, all non-trivial functional
dependencies are listed. The underlined attributes are the respective primary keys.

Schema I: Registration (rollno, courses)
Field ‘courses’ is a set-valued attribute containing the set of courses a student has
registered for.
Non-trivial functional dependency:
rollno → courses

Schema II: Registration (rollno, courseid, email)
Non-trivial functional dependencies:
rollno, courseid → email
email → rollno

Schema III: Registration (rollno, courseid, marks, grade)
Non-trivial functional dependencies:
rollno, courseid → marks, grade
marks → grade

Schema IV: Registration (rollno, courseid, credit)
Non-trivial functional dependencies:
rollno, courseid → credit
courseid → credit

Which one of the relational schemas above is in 3NF but not in BCNF?
questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms
questions.explaination: In Schema II, the functional dependencies are $rollno \to email$ and $email \to rollno$. The candidate keys are $\{rollno, courseid\}$ and $\{email, courseid\}$. In $email \to rollno$, the left side is not a superkey (violating BCNF), but the right side $rollno$ is a prime attribute (satisfying 3NF). Hence Schema II is in 3NF but not in BCNF.

    \item[Schema IV:] $R_4(A, B, C)$ with FDs: $AB \to C, C \to A$
\end{itemize}
Which one of the relational schemas is in 3NF but not in BCNF?

questions.question_text: In a relational data model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: A relation with only two attributes is always in BCNF.
options.B: If all attributes of a relation are prime attributes, then the relation is in BCNF.
options.C: Every relation has at least one non-prime attribute.

questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms
questions.explaination: For any binary relation $R(A, B)$, the only possible non-trivial functional dependencies are $A \to B$ or $B \to A$. In either case, the left-hand side is a superkey of $R$, satisfying the definition of Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF).

Consider the relational database with the following four schemas and their
respective instances.
Student(sNo, sName, dNo) Dept(dNo, dName)
Course(cNo, cName, dNo) Register(sNo, cNo)
SQL Query:

SELECT * FROM Student AS S WHERE NOT EXIST
(SELECT cNo FROM Course WHERE dNo = “D01”

EXCEPT
SELECT cNo FROM Register WHERE sNo = S.sNo)
The number of rows returned by the above SQL query is___________.
questions.subtopic: Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL
questions.explaination: The nested subquery with `EXCEPT` and `NOT EXISTS` expresses relational division: it finds students who have registered for every course offered by department 'D01'. In the database instance, exactly 2 students satisfy this condition.

In a B+ tree, the requirement of at least half-full (50%) node occupancy is relaxed
for which one of the following cases?
questions.subtopic: File organization, indexing (e.g., B and B+ trees)
questions.explaination: In a $\text{B}^+$ tree, every node except the root node must satisfy the minimum occupancy constraint of being at least half full ($	ext{at least } \lceil p/2 \rceil$ child pointers). questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about a relation R in first normal form (1NF)
is/are TRUE ?

options.A: R can have a multi-attribute key
options.B: R cannot have a foreign key
options.C: R cannot have a composite attribute
options.D: R cannot have more than one candidate key

questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms
questions.explaination: A relation is in 1NF if and only if all attribute values are atomic, which explicitly forbids composite or multi-valued attributes (making (C) TRUE). 1NF places no limitation on candidate keys having multiple attributes (multi-attribute keys are fully permitted, making (A) TRUE) or the presence of foreign keys.

questions.question_text:
The symbol → indicates functional dependency in the context of a relational
database. Which of the following options is/are TRUE?
questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms
questions.explaination: By Armstrong's decomposition axiom, $(X, Y) \to (Z, W)$ implies $(X, Y) \to Z$ (B is TRUE). By Armstrong's transitivity axiom, $X \to Y$ and $Y \to Z$ implies $X \to Z$ (D is TRUE). By pseudotransitivity, $(X, Y) \to Z$ and $W \to Y$ implies $(X, W) \to Z$ (C is TRUE). Decomposing the left-hand side determinant is invalid in general (A is FALSE).

questions.question_text:
A functional dependency 𝐹:⁡𝑋→𝑌 is termed as a useful functional dependency if
and only if it satisfies all the following three conditions:
• 𝑋 is not the empty set.
• 𝑌 is not the empty set.
• Intersection of 𝑋 and 𝑌 is the empty set.

For a relation 𝑅 with 4 attributes, the total number of possible useful functional
dependencies is ________
questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms
questions.explaination: For each attribute $A$ among the 4 attributes, there are 3 mutually exclusive choices: $A \in X$, $A \in Y$, or $A \notin (X \cup Y)$, giving $3^4 = 81$ pairs of disjoint sets $(X, Y)$. We subtract cases where $X = \emptyset$ ($2^4 = 16$), where $Y = \emptyset$ ($2^4 = 16$), and add back the double-subtracted case where $X = Y = \emptyset$ ($1$). Total useful FDs $= 81 - 16 - 16 + 1 = 50$.
questions.question_text_latex:

name and the team-id of the player, respectively
Which ONE of the following tuple relational calculus queries returns the name of the
players who play for the team having 𝑡𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒 as ′𝑀𝐼′?

options.A: { 𝑝. 𝑝𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒 | 𝑝∈𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑦𝑒𝑟𝑠∧∃𝑡 (𝑡∈𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚𝑠∧𝑝. 𝑡𝑖𝑑= 𝑡. 𝑡𝑖𝑑∧𝑡. 𝑡𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒= ′𝑀𝐼′)}

questions.question_text:
Consider a relational schema 𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚(𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒, 𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑦, 𝑜𝑤𝑛𝑒𝑟), with functional
dependencies {𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒→𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑦, 𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒→𝑜𝑤𝑛𝑒𝑟}.
The relation 𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚 is decomposed into two relations, 𝑡1(𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒, 𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑦) and
𝑡2(𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒, 𝑜𝑤𝑛𝑒𝑟). Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

options.A: The relation 𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚 is NOT in BCNF.
options.B: The relations 𝑡1 and 𝑡2 are in BCNF.
options.C: The decomposition constitutes a lossless join.
options.D:
The relation 𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚 is NOT in 3NF.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms
questions.explaination: In $team$, $name$ is a candidate key since $name^+ = \{name, city, owner\}$. Since every FD has a superkey on the LHS, $team$ was already in BCNF and 3NF (A and D are false). In $t_1$ and $t_2$, $name$ is the primary key, so both are in BCNF (B is true). The common attribute $R_1 \cap R_2 = \{name\}$ is a key of both $t_1$ and $t_2$, ensuring a lossless join (C is true).
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a relational schema $team(name, city, owner)$, with functional dependencies $\{name \to city, name \to owner\}$. The relation $team$ is decomposed into two relations, $t_1(name, city)$ and $t_2(name, owner)$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

options_latex.A: The relation $team$ is NOT in BCNF.
options_latex.B: The relations $t_1$ and $t_2$ are in BCNF.
options_latex.C: The decomposition constitutes a lossless join.

questions.question_text:
An audit of a banking transactions system has found that on an earlier occasion, two
joint holders of account 𝐴 attempted simultaneous transfers of Rs. 10000 each from
account 𝐴 to account 𝐵. Both transactions read the same value, Rs. 11000, as the
initial balance in 𝐴 and were allowed to go through. 𝐵 was credited Rs. 10000 twice.
𝐴 was debited only once and ended up with a balance of Rs. 1000.
Which of the following properties is/are certain to have been violated by the
system?
questions.subtopic: Transactions and concurrency control: ACID properties
questions.explaination: Both transactions read the same uncommitted state and overwrote each other (lost update anomaly), violating Isolation. The final balance violates the database invariant (starting 11000 debited $2 \times 10000$ cannot yield 1000), violating Consistency.
questions.question_text_latex: An audit of a banking transactions system has found that on an earlier occasion, two joint holders of account $A$ attempted simultaneous transfers of Rs. 10000 each from account $A$ to account $B$. Both transactions read the same value, Rs. 11000, as the initial balance in $A$ and were allowed to go through. $B$ was credited Rs. 10000 twice. $A$ was debited only once and ended up with a balance of Rs. 1000. Which of the following properties is/are certain to have been violated by the system?

options.D:
R2 is NOT in 3NF

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Integrity constraints, normal forms: 3NF and BCNF
questions.explaination: A schema is in 3NF if for every non-trivial FD $X \to Y$, either $X$ is a superkey or $Y$ consists of prime attributes. Here, both schemas contain dependencies where the LHS is not a superkey and the RHS has non-prime attributes, so neither is in 3NF.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following relational schema:
Students (rollno: integer, name: string, age: integer, cgpa: real)
Courses (courseno: integer, cname: string, credits: integer)
Enrolled (rollno: integer, courseno: integer, grade: string)
Which of the following options is/are correct SQL query/queries to retrieve the
names of the students enrolled in course number (i.e., courseno) 1470?

options.A:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470
AND E.rollno = S.rollno);
options.B:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S
WHERE SIZEOF (SELECT * FROM Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470
AND E.rollno = S.rollno) > 0;
options.C:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S
WHERE 0 < (SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470
AND E.rollno = S.rollno);
options.D:
SELECT S.name
FROM Students S NATURAL JOIN Enrolled E
WHERE E.courseno = 1470;

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Relational model: SQL queries and joins
questions.explaination: Queries A, C, and D all correctly return the names of students enrolled in course 1470 using EXISTS, COUNT, and natural join respectively. Query B is invalid because SQL does not have a `SIZEOF` operator.
